articles.title: Angel Reese oozes positivity despite Game 7 loss, although she might regret one specific WNBA Finals moment
articles.standfirst: Reese and the Atlanta Dream fell just short against the Golden State Valkyries for the WNBA championship.
articles.summary: Reese and the Atlanta Dream fell just short against the Golden State Valkyries for the WNBA championship.
articles.body:
A magical 2026 season for the Atlanta Dream has come to an end in the most heartbreaking fashion. Going toe-to-toe with the Golden State Valkyries in the Bay Area, Angel Reese and co. lost by five points in Game 7 and came away from the WNBA Finals empty-handed. Still, there's plenty to be optimistic about.

Reese herself knows that very well. After two brutal collective seasons with the Chicago Sky , Reese got her first taste of playoff basketball in her first season with the Dream, and they made it all the way to the final possible game together. That's more than enough for Reese to continue dreaming big despite the tough loss .

Angel Reese: Atlanta Dream "changed my life"

During her postgame press conference, Reese made sure to reiterate her gratefulness for the Dream organization and her teammates . She was clearly battling a lot of emotions, but she remained positive .

I mean, yeah, it's tough. Especially with the great group that, honestly [it's been an] honor to battle with all year. They changed my life, and I'm so grateful for them, and I'm so thankful for them. It is tough in the moment, but we'll be back. I always say, delayed not denied. This is only Year 3... I'm just really grateful that I got to go to war with this group and I would do it again, all over again.

Reese made a big impact on the boards with 12 rebounds and was her usual dominant self on the defensive end. She was only able to muster eight points in Game 7 after struggling offensively the past three games.

Her haters have now come out in full force, pinpointing a karmic moment where Reese was teasing the Valkyries during the Dream's 97-71 victory in Game 3 . Since then, it all went downhill on the offensive end for her.

Reese has nothing to apologize for, though; that confident attitude is what got her and the Dream this far. She isn't going to change it, and the Dream don't want her to.

articles.title: Angel Reese opts for a comfortable look before the WNBA Finals heartbreak that ended Atlanta’s title dream
articles.standfirst: The Dream star arrived at the decisive WNBA Finals game in a sporty, street-style outfit that balanced comfort and style.
articles.summary: The Dream star arrived at the decisive WNBA Finals game in a sporty, street-style outfit that balanced comfort and style.
articles.body:
Halloween ended in celebration for Golden State and heartbreak for Atlanta. Before taking the court for Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, Angel Reese stepped out in a look that prioritized comfort without sacrificing style .

Angel Reese’s sporty-chic look before the decisive game

For the occasion, Reese chose a fitted white long-sleeve shirt paired with wide-leg gray track pants featuring three white stripes down the sides . Black sneakers completed the outfit, with a neutral color palette that kept the look simple and urban.

Her accessories added personality to the ensemble. The basketball star wore black sunglasses with chunky frames, carried an oversized black bag, and sported white wired headphones . She also held a cream-colored reusable water bottle, while her long, wavy hair added volume to an outfit that let the basics do all the work.

Atlanta dreamed of a title, but Golden State took it all

As Reese prepared for the biggest game of the season, the Atlanta Dream were looking to cap off a campaign that had already marked a turning point for the franchise. The team finished the regular season with a 30-14 record and reached the Finals after defeating the New York Liberty in the semifinals .

The championship series had its share of twists and turns. Atlanta took a 2-1 lead and forced a winner-take-all Game 7 after defeating Golden State in front of its home crowd in Game 6. With the championship just one win away, the Dream had a chance to make franchise history. However, the Golden State Valkyries ultimately prevailed 68-63 on Saturday, October 31, at Chase Center in San Francisco .

The deciding game also made WNBA history, marking the first time the league’s Finals had gone to a Game 7.

Angel Reese also made her mark in the Finals

Although the outcome was not what she had hoped for, Reese wrapped up an impressive first season with Atlanta after arriving from Chicago . During the regular season, she averaged 16.4 points and 12.1 rebounds per game, was named Defensive Player of the Year, and finished seventh in MVP voting.

In the Finals, the forward set a new WNBA record for rebounds in a championship series, finishing with 78. In Game 7, she recorded 12 rebounds and two blocks, while her offensive production was limited to eight points .

articles.title: Gabby Williams' dig at those who only focus on Caitlin Clark or A'ja Wilson after winning the WNBA championship
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream to the title on Saturday
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream to the title on Saturday
articles.body:
G abby Williams had just won the WNBA championship and Finals MVP , but her message after the Golden State Valkyries ' historic victory was aimed at those who had doubted the expansion franchise as she highlighted the collective effort that had delivered the title. Williams scored just two points in the first half of the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history but by the final buzzer, she had helped the Valkyries defeat the Atlanta Dream 68-63, completing an extraordinary journey for a team competing in only its second season.

Rather than celebrate individual achievements, her comments offered a reminder that championship success does not always depend on having the biggest individual stars as attention across the WNBA frequently gravitates towards players such as Caitlin Clark and A'ja Wilson . And Williams wanted recognition for the culture built in Golden State after their landmark accomplishment against the Angel Reese -led Dream on Saturday, October 31. "Man, all it took was good people," Williams said. "That's it. All we heard last year, 'We don't have no stars. We don't have no talent.' “We got good people. We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game. “They don't care about scoring. They just want to play defense and rebound and just do whatever it takes. And we just built a beautiful culture here."

Nakase gamble pays off as Valkyries achieve golden moment in the WNBA

The criticism began during the inaugural campaign, when questions surrounded their ability to compete with established elite but they became the first expansion team in WNBA history to reach the playoffs in its first season. Now they’re champions. Case closed. And part of that reason is coach Natalie Nakase established the team's defensive identity from the beginning of training camp as she refused to let players pick up basketballs for the first three days. Concentrating entirely on defensive principles. Golden State subsequently allowed a league-low 75.1 points per game and that commitment was particularly evident in the Finals. After falling behind Atlanta 2-1, Nakase changed her starting lineup, promoting Kaila Charles and Tiffany Hayes while moving Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini to the bench. The players accepted the decision without complaint, and Golden State won the next two games to take control before Williams later delivered when the championship was on the line. After her quiet first half, she scored the Valkyries ' final 11 points of the third quarter and finished with 30. Her decisive three-pointer answered Rhyne Howard 's game-tying basket with 2:41 remaining. Owner Joe Lacob had promised a championship within five years when Golden State received its expansion franchise and the Valkyries delivered well ahead of schedule in their second season. Now everyone is taking them seriously.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark turns Halloween into a night of scares with a simple mask and a few tricks
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark traded a big Halloween party for a night at home, where she decided to scare trick-or-treaters with nothing more than a mask. The Fever star managed to send some of the younger children running, but the older kids weren't nearly as impressed by her costume and seemed harder to frighten. None of them realized the person behind the mask was Clark herself, something that might have made their reactions a little more enthusiastic. Aliyah Boston, meanwhile, gave Clark's Halloween prank her seal of approval. She was even cozier than her teammate, relaxing in bed when Clark called her on FaceTime, clearly excited to show off her scary mask. The Fever teammates appear to be enjoying a quieter offseason after a WNBA season that didn't go entirely as planned.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark makes easy money when she shows, with just a gesture, why she's the face of the WNBA
articles.standfirst: Clark continues to stay active during the Indiana Fever’s WNBA offseason
articles.summary: Clark continues to stay active during the Indiana Fever’s WNBA offseason
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark needed just one shot to turn a MrBeast charity challenge into a $90,000 donation, giving fans another reminder of the shooting ability that has made her one of basketball 's biggest attractions.

The Indiana Fever star connected from the logo after Jimmy Donaldson missed his attempt as the moment appeared in MrBeast’s latest YouTube video, released Saturday, featuring LeBron James, Erling Haaland, Simone Biles and Alysa Liu .

Clark took part at a Fever practice court, where the challenge was simple: make a shot from the logo to win money for charity as Donaldson went first but failed to find the basket.

Clark then stepped up and delivered, completing the challenge with a shot that demonstrated the range and confidence behind her reputation as a sharpshooter and a clip shared by a fan account on X.com, formerly Twitter, quickly attracted attention.

One supporter described the attempt as “Light work and easy money for Caitlin.” A second said, "Unexpected collab, Imma go watch the YT vid now.”

And a third commented, "Mr.Beast came for a three-point contest and left with a $90K lesson. Caitlin really made half-court shots look casual.”

The moment also came as Clark continues to make the most of her offseason, with several projects keeping her in the public eye beyond basketball.

Signature shoe launch leaves fans frustrated

Clark is scheduled to appear on ABC's Good Morning America on November 3 to promote her children's book, EXTRAordinary! A Little Extra to Reach Big Dreams, which is due to be released the same day.

Her partnership with Nike has also generated considerable attention following the launch of her first signature shoe, the Caitlin 1. The latest release, the Halloween-themed Jinx edition, arrived on October 30, but its limited availability left some supporters frustrated.

The design takes inspiration from a cat named Jinx that frightened Clark when she was younger. Nike's promotional video, narrated by Nick Offerman , explained how she turned that childhood fear into the inspiration for a sneaker.

The shoes feature black, ghost green and mint tones, with green cat eyes on the back of the tongue. Their soles and lower trim also glow in the dark, giving the Halloween release a distinctive finish.

However, access was restricted to Nike SNKRS Exclusive Access, leaving many fans unable to buy a pair. Clark shared the promotional video on X with the message, “Best of luck getting these,” but the response included complaints about the release process.

One frustrated supporter wrote online, “I would love to thank Nike for hiding this release and blocking true fans and collectors from getting them. If you weren’t one of the very few lucky ones, you can buy them for over $300 on eBay today.”

Another described the launch as “absolute BS,” while others questioned why the sneakers had been so difficult to purchase.

The Caitlin 1 first arrived on October 1 in Caitlin Blue and Warning Code editions, priced at $140 for adult sizes. Midnight Fever followed on October 14, while the Jinx edition retailed for $150.

More releases are planned, with Cave Stone scheduled for November 3, Ice Cold on December 1 and Purple Venom on December 12.

articles.title: Angel Reese missed out on WNBA championship with Atlanta Dream, but her mother ensured the loss hurt less
articles.standfirst: Reese's historic postseason ended in disappointment, although footage of the star leaving the court with her mother quickly captured fans' attention
articles.summary: Reese's historic postseason ended in disappointment, although footage of the star leaving the court with her mother quickly captured fans' attention
articles.body:
A ngel Reese 's pursuit of her first WNBA championship ended in disappointment on Saturday night, but the Atlanta Dream forward didn't have to face the aftermath alone as her mother accompanied her off the court following a heartbreaking Game 7 defeat.

The Dream suffered a 68-63 loss to the Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center, bringing an end to a remarkable postseason campaign that had taken Reese within touching distance of the biggest prize in women's basketball.

As Golden State celebrated its first championship, cameras captured Reese leaving the floor alongside her mother, Angel Webb Reese , in footage shared by Bleacher Report that quickly attracted attention across social media.

The moment provided a touching contrast to the celebrations unfolding around them, with supporters recognizing the importance of family during one of the most disappointing nights of Reese 's young professional career.

Reese finished the deciding contest with eight points, 12 rebounds and two blocks, but Atlanta could not overcome an inspired second-half performance from Golden State's Gabby Williams , who scored 30 points to secure the championship.

The emotional scenes prompted an immediate response from supporters, many of whom praised the bond between Reese and her mother rather than focusing solely on the result.

"Win or lose, Mom's always gonna be there," one fan wrote in response to the video. Another supporter expressed confidence that Reese would eventually claim a championship, writing: "Remember this moment when my girl comes back to win the Chip next year!"

The reaction reflected the growing appreciation for Reese 's achievements during a season in which she established herself among the WNBA's most influential players.

Despite the Game 7 defeat, Reese made history by becoming the first player to accumulate at least 100 points and 50 rebounds in a single WNBA Finals series.

She finished the seven-game contest averaging 14.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and three assists, having delivered a 30-point, 16-rebound performance earlier in the series.

Her outstanding defensive contributions also earned her the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year award, further underlining her development during her third professional season.

Atlanta Dream left to reflect

Atlanta's disappointment was particularly difficult given the position the team had established throughout the postseason.

The Dream swept their opening two playoff series against Washington and New York before taking a 2-1 lead against Golden State in the Finals.

Although Atlanta recovered from consecutive defeats to force Game 7, the team could not convert a 30-24 halftime advantage into victory.

Jordin Canada led the Dream with 18 points, while Allisha Gray contributed 16, but Williams ' decisive scoring performance ultimately secured Golden State's first championship.

Reese will now enter the offseason reflecting on a campaign that delivered individual recognition and a historic Finals appearance without the championship she had pursued.

Yet the image of her walking away alongside her mother offered a reminder that, even after the most painful defeats, the support surrounding an athlete can matter as much as anything achieved on the court.

articles.summary: The Fever star skipped the big Halloween celebrations and found a different way to have fun

C aitlin Clark found her own way to enjoy Halloween despite not being part of the WNBA Finals action that day. Instead of heading to a big costume party, the Indiana Fever star spent the night at home, getting her fun by scaring trick-or-treaters with a simple mask.

articles.standfirst: Golden State finally has another basketball champion, and Curry couldn't contain his excitement
articles.summary: Golden State finally has another basketball champion, and Curry couldn't contain his excitement
articles.body:
S teph Curry looked like he had been waiting a long time for this moment. The Golden State Valkyries delivered a historic championship for the franchise and the Bay Area, where fans had been desperate to celebrate another title.

The Warriors' recent decline has drawn plenty of criticism, with some questioning whether Golden State is doing enough to build a championship contender around Curry before his career comes to an end . Others believe the franchise should let him go so he can pursue another title elsewhere, arguing that the Warriors may no longer be in a position to give him what he needs.

The Bay Area finds an unexpected path to glory

The wait for another championship had become frustrating for Golden State fans, but the possibility of the women's team delivering that moment was not something many had expected so soon . The Valkyries had only been around for two seasons, making a title seem unlikely by the numbers, but they proved otherwise. Curry nearly ran out of breath celebrating their victory over the Atlanta Dream.

The Golden State Valkyries went from an expansion team still establishing its identity to WNBA champions in just two seasons , becoming the fastest expansion team in major North American professional sports to win a championship after defeating Atlanta 68-63 in Game 7 of the Finals. Gabby Williams led the way with a career-defining 30-point performance, securing the franchise's first championship.

Curry never stopped showing his support

The championship also answered questions about whether the young franchise had enough star power to compete at the highest level. Curry believed in the team throughout the season, making appearances at several games to show his support and lift the players' spirits when things were not going their way.

That support carried into a seven-game series and ultimately the franchise's first title. For a team that was still facing doubts about its talent and ability to compete just a year ago, the championship was a definitive response.

The Valkyries have now given the Bay Area another reason to celebrate , and perhaps their success can bring some hope to the Warriors as well. At least Curry's reaction suggests he is enjoying the moment.

articles.title: Angel Reese's first post after losing the WNBA Finals could carry a cryptic message for Caitlin Clark
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star reflected on what it means to play in the Finals in just her third year in the WNBA. Although she did not mention Caitlin Clark, one phrase in her post once again fueled comparisons between the two.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star reflected on what it means to play in the Finals in just her third year in the WNBA. Although she did not mention Caitlin Clark, one phrase in her post once again fueled comparisons between the two.
articles.body:
Angel Reese took almost 24 hours to post her first message after losing the WNBA Finals. The Atlanta Dream player fell on Saturday to the Golden State Valkyries by 68-63 in Game 7 and, the following day, shared on Instagram a reflection on her season and how close she came to winning the title.

Amid a message centered on pride in what had been achieved, there was one phrase that especially caught attention: "I realize that not many get to experience this in their third year in the league."

Reese did not mention Caitlin Clark , but the reference to her third year as a professional reignited comparisons with the Indiana Fever star.

The phrase that put Caitlin Clark back in the spotlight

Reese spoke after the loss and acknowledged that she was still affected by having lost the final, although she highlighted what it meant to reach the Finals in just her third season in the league.

Through her social media, she said she was in shock over how the championship ended. She later assured that she was "MORE THAN PROUD" and that she had nothing to reproach herself for.

In the post, mentioning her third year takes on special significance because of her history with Caitlin Clark . Both entered the WNBA in 2024, after being at the center of one of the most talked-about rivalries in college basketball. Since then, their careers have followed different paths, but they continue to be compared by fans and the media.

However, there is an important distinction: Reese did not name Clark or frame her message as a response to her. The comparison arises from the context of their respective careers.

Reese is already thinking about next season

In her post, the player also made it clear that the defeat does not change her goals or her desire to keep competing at the highest level. Far from seeing it as a definitive failure, she views it as an opportunity to learn and prepare for what comes next.

"Every defeat is a lesson and, sometimes, it’s not a NO, but simply a NOT YET. It’s a delay, not a rejection. Believe me, I REALLY WANT more", she wrote. With those words, Reese made it clear that the experience in the Finals has not diminished her ambition and that she remains determined to fight for the first championship of her career.

The season also brought her significant individual recognition.

Reese was selected as an All-Star for the third consecutive year, made the All-WNBA Second Team, and won the Defensive Player of the Year award. In addition, she set historic records in the competition during the season and the playoffs.

The ending, however, was painful. In Game 7 against Golden State, Reese finished with eight points, 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal, and two blocks in 33 minutes. The Valkyries prevailed 68-63 and captured the first title in their history, just in their second season in the league.

The player closed her message with a phrase that sums up her intention to return to compete for the championship: "Back to work! See you in six months". The defeat still weighs heavily, but Reese has already made it clear that her goal remains intact

articles.title: The controversial video haunting Angel Reese after losing the WNBA Finals: “Who did it?”
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese faces fresh criticism after Dave Portnoy shares a brutal compilation of her Finals mistakes
articles.summary: Angel Reese faces fresh criticism after Dave Portnoy shares a brutal compilation of her Finals mistakes
articles.body:
Angel Reese’s first appearance in the WNBA Finals ended in heartbreak, but the Atlanta Dream star has found herself dealing with another wave of criticism after Dave Portnoy took aim at her following the championship defeat.

The Barstool Sports founder, a longtime critic of Reese and outspoken Caitlin Clark supporter, wasted little time reacting to Atlanta’s Game 7 loss. Taking to X, formerly Twitter, Portnoy shared a compilation featuring some of Reese’s missed shots and mistakes throughout the Finals.

“Yoooo….who made this video?” Portnoy wrote alongside the footage, adding that Reese was “0-1 lifetime in WNBA Finals.”

The compilation featured clips of Reese discussing her championship ambitions and displaying her confidence during games. Those moments were followed by footage of missed attempts, turnovers and air balls, creating a video that quickly attracted attention following Atlanta’s defeat.

The criticism came after the Golden State Valkyries defeated the Dream 68-63 on Halloween, securing the championship in a decisive seventh game. Atlanta had managed to extend the series after forcing Game 7, but couldn't complete its comeback and fell just short of lifting the trophy.

Reese finished the deciding contest with eight points, 12 rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Although she had delivered impressive performances earlier in the series, her offensive production declined during several important games.

The forward recorded double-doubles in each of the first three Finals contests, helping Atlanta establish an early advantage.

However, she struggled to maintain that scoring consistency in Games 4 and 5. She bounced back during Game 6 with 15 points and 14 rebounds before another difficult offensive outing in the championship decider.

Angel Reese receives support from Wendell Carter Jr. after Finals heartbreak

Portnoy's latest comments also brought renewed attention to the rivalry between Reese and Clark , which dates back to their college basketball careers. Reese's LSU team defeated Clark's Iowa squad in the 2023 NCAA championship game, and their competitive relationship has continued to attract considerable attention in the WNBA.

Portnoy has repeatedly criticized Reese over her performances and on-court behavior. However, the Dream forward hasn't allowed the latest criticism to overshadow her ambitions.

Almost a day after the defeat, Reese addressed the heartbreaking result through an Instagram post, reflecting on her season and expressing pride in what Atlanta had accomplished.

“Every loss is a lesson,” Reese wrote, explaining that sometimes the answer isn't no, but simply not yet. She concluded her message with a determined statement: “Delayed, not denied. Trust me, I'm HUNGRY for more.”

Her boyfriend, NBA player Wendell Carter Jr. , also showed his support in the comments section, leaving two encouraging messages: “You will prevail” and “Just getting started.”

Reese also addressed the team's future during her postgame media session, making it clear that she believes Atlanta can return to championship contention.

“It is tough in the moment, but we'll be back,” she said, reiterating her belief that the opportunity to win a title hasn't disappeared.

The Finals loss was undoubtedly a disappointing ending, but Reese remains determined to use the experience as motivation. With another season ahead, the Dream will have time to regroup, evaluate their shortcomings and prepare for another championship challenge.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham, once desperately needing a second job to survive, lands a $665K payday
articles.standfirst: What once seemed impossible during her early WNBA days has become part of a very different financial reality for Cunnigham
articles.summary: What once seemed impossible during her early WNBA days has become part of a very different financial reality for Cunnigham
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham's financial situation looks very different today. When she entered the WNBA in 2019, her rookie salary was barely enough to cover her expenses, leaving her wondering whether she needed a second job to make ends meet.

During an appearance on Theo Von's podcast, the Indiana Fever guard recalled earning around $28,000 after taxes in her first season. Despite reaching her goal of becoming a professional basketball player, the financial reality was far from what she had expected.

A major change in WNBA salaries

Seven years later, which seems like a long time, Cunningham secured a one-year, $665,000 contract to remain with Indiana for the 2026 season. The payday marks a significant change from her rookie earnings and reflects the financial progress made across the league. Although there's still exists a major gap between the NBA and the WNBA .

The new collective bargaining agreement, ratified in March 2026, increased the WNBA salary cap from $1.5 million to $7 million . The changes have given players access to salaries that were difficult to imagine when Cunningham first entered the league.

Building wealth beyond basketball

Cunningham has also developed income opportunities outside the court. Her partnerships with brands such as Adidas, Arby's and Quest Nutrition have expanded her commercial presence, while her work in sports media and podcasting has opened additional doors.

She has also invested in real estate, purchasing vacation properties that can generate income beyond her playing career. After once considering another job to support herself, Cunningham now has a much stronger financial foundation and more opportunities to plan for life after basketball.

articles.title: Michael Jordan recognizes real greatness: Cold reminder for Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark's ring pursuit
articles.standfirst: Michael Jordan gives his respect to the WNBA champions
articles.summary: Michael Jordan gives his respect to the WNBA champions
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries wrote a new chapter in WNBA history by capturing their first championship after defeating the Atlanta Dream 4-3 in an unforgettable series. The star of the night was Gabby Williams , who earned Finals MVP honors after averaging nearly 20 points throughout the series and delivering a historic 30-point performance in Game 7 .

Her incredible performance did not go unnoticed and caught the attention of one of the greatest legends in sports history: Michael Jordan . The former Chicago Bulls superstar and six-time NBA champion sent Williams a message congratulating her on the title, according to the player herself in a post shared by ESPN reporter Kendra Andrews .

The recognition comes as no surprise, as Williams was the key piece behind Golden State’s championship victory. The Valkyries star dominated on both ends of the floor, carrying the team’s offense while making a major defensive impact in the biggest game of the season.

Twenty-eight of her 30 points came in the second half, setting a record in WNBA Finals history and accounting for nearly half of G olden State’s 68 total points in the game. The Valkyries entered halftime trailing by six points and fell behind by as many as nine during the third quarter, but Williams stepped up when her team needed her most.

The star scored 15 points in the third quarter and 13 more in the fourth to lead the comeback and deliver Golden State the first championship in franchise history. Along with her 30 points, she finished with an impressive stat line of three rebounds, four blocks, two assists and two steals, in one of the most memorable individual performances in WNBA Finals history.

The second-leading scorer for the Valkyries was Tiffany Hayes , who added 11 points, while Veronica Burton recorded a double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds. Williams finished the game shooting 10-of-23 from the field, but her impact went far beyond the box score.

After becoming a champion and Finals MVP, receiving a personal message from Michael Jordan was the perfect recognition for a player who just delivered one of the most important moments in the young history of the Valkyries.

articles.title: Angel Reese announces sudden six-month break after brutal WNBA Finals loss
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese is stepping away for six months after a heartbreaking WNBA Finals loss, focusing on rest, family and rebuilding ahead of her return.
articles.summary: Angel Reese is stepping away for six months after a heartbreaking WNBA Finals loss, focusing on rest, family and rebuilding ahead of her return.
articles.body:
The end of a season usually opens a period of rest and reflection for any athlete, but Angel Reese appears determined to make the most of her time away from the court. After a historic campaign in which she led the Atlanta Dream to their first WNBA Finals appearance since 2013 , the league star is planning a quieter offseason focused on her personal well-being and projects outside basketball.

“I won’t be doing my podcast this offseason, but you can expect some vlogs from time to time. So subscribe to my YouTube,” Reese posted on her private Barbie Archives Instagram account.

“Florida will be my home and I will be there resting, working out, continuing to quietly work on my personal brand, and supporting/loving my partner. These are things I love to do that bring me so much PEACE.”

Reese’s partner, Wendell Carter Jr. , plays for the Orlando Magic and spends the NBA regular season in Florida . As part of this new chapter, the forward also decided to take a six-month break from her podcast "Unapologetically Angel", which had remained active until last April 3 .

The decision comes after a year of tremendous physical and emotional demands. After being traded from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream during the offseason, Reese became a key piece for the team, leading them to a 30-14 record and the No. 4 seed in the standings. She also broke several rebounding records and was named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year .

The forward was also instrumental in Atlanta’s historic playoff run. The Dream won their first two playoff series to reach the Finals, where they ultimately fell to the Golden State Valkyries after becoming the first team in WNBA Finals history to push a series to a Game 7 .

The truth is that Reese started the Finals playing at an elite level. In the first three games of the series, she was one of the best players on the floor and even took responsibility for Atlanta’s Game 1 loss against Golden State .

In Game 2 , she recorded 30 points, 16 rebounds and two blocks , while in Game 3 she posted a double-double wit h 21 points and 12 rebounds . Both games ended with victories for the Dream. However, her offensive production dramatically declined during the decisive stretch of the series.

In the final four games of the Finals, Reese scored in double figures only once. She averaged 9.5 points per game, shooting just 26.6% from the field while committing 4.7 turnovers per contest.

She also faced criticism for some of her gestures during the series. In Game 3, Reese performed the “too small” and “you can’t f* with me”** celebrations toward Valkyries rookie Amanita Gueye, moments that were brought back into the spotlight after Atlanta ultimately lost the championship.

Despite everything, Reese made it clear after Game 7 that she still believes in her team and expects the Dream to compete for a title again.

“It’s tough, especially with a good group, a great group, that I’ve honestly been a head on it to battle with all year,” she said during the press conference.

“I always say delayed, not denied, and this is only year three. They got a lot more years left, too. But I’m just really grateful that I got to go to war with this group, and I would do it again, all over again.”

Now that the season is over, Reese will use the offseason to recharge, focus on her personal life and continue building her brand. Although her podcast break will temporarily reduce her public presence, the WNBA star is expected to remain at the center of attention very soon.

“I always say delayed, not denied, and this is only year three. They got a lot more years left, too. But I’m just really grateful that I got to go to war with this group, and I would do it again, all over again.”

Now that the season is over, Reese will use the offseason to recharge, focus on her personal life and continue building her brand. Although her podcast break will temporarily reduce her public presence, the WNBA star is expected to remain at the center of attention very soon.

articles.title: Kylie Kelce shamelessly tries to recruit Caitlin Clark for Philadelphia's new WNBA team
articles.standfirst: Jason Kelce's wife took advantage of her conversation with the Indiana Fever star to try to convince her to join the franchise that will debut in 2030. Clark's response left the conversation open.
articles.summary: Jason Kelce's wife took advantage of her conversation with the Indiana Fever star to try to convince her to join the franchise that will debut in 2030. Clark's response left the conversation open.
articles.body:
Kylie Kelce didn’t want to miss the opportunity. During her meeting with Caitlin Clark on Not Gonna Lie , Jason Kelce’s wife tried to convince the Indiana Fever star to join Philadelphia’s future team, a franchise scheduled to debut in the WNBA in 2030. The host even admitted that she is willing to work several years in advance to make it happen.

The conversation took place in the special podcast episode published this Tuesday, November 3. Clark, 24, responded humorously to the proposal and even mentioned her agent, although she did not announce any concrete interest in leaving Indiana.

Kylie Kelce is already thinking of Caitlin Clark for Philadelphia’s team

"As a lifelong Philadelphia resident, I also spoke with Dawn Staley about the WNBA team we’ll have in Philly in 2030. I have five years to do it, but I’m going to start right now. How can I recruit you to Philadelphia?", Kylie asked the player.

Clark did not rule out the possibility, but she also gave no signs of preparing for a team change. "I’m going to have to talk to my agent", she replied with a laugh. The response was enough for Kelce to press on with her goal: "I’m going to play the long game to get the best in the world to come to Philadelphia. I’ll come back to this."

The new WNBA franchise will debut in 2030

The arrival of a professional women's team to Philadelphia is now confirmed. The WNBA and the NBA officially approved the league's expansion on April 9, 2026. The franchise will begin competing in 2030 and will be based in the southern part of the city.

This is not the first time Kylie has tried to attract a star from the competition. In a previous conversation with A"ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces standout , she also took the opportunity to talk to her about the Philadelphia project and ask how she could convince her to play there. The host seems determined to help build a competitive roster even before the team plays its first game.

For now, Clark remains tied to the Indiana Fever and has not expressed any intention of changing franchises. In fact, when speaking about Philadelphia, she gave one final response that sums up the lighthearted tone of the exchange: if she doesn’t end up playing there, she will at least have to visit the city once or twice per season as an opponent.

articles.title: "Dear Caitlin Clark mob...": Fans obsessed with Angel Reese’s defeat in the WNBA Finals get a major reality check
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese's Finals struggles spark another heated clash between rival fanbases
articles.summary: Angel Reese's Finals struggles spark another heated clash between rival fanbases
articles.body:
Angel Reese’s disappointing finish to the 2026 WNBA Finals has sparked another heated debate among basketball fans, prompting former NBA player Etan Thomas to call out supporters who’ve repeatedly targeted the Atlanta Dream star.

Following Atlanta’s 68-63 Game 7 defeat against the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday, Reese became the subject of considerable criticism across social media.

Thomas , however, wasn't impressed with the celebrations surrounding her struggles and questioned why certain Caitlin Clark supporters were so invested in another player's disappointment.

In a lengthy Threads post on Monday, Thomas sarcastically congratulated the so-called Caitlin Clark mob for celebrating Reese’s defeat before pointing out that their favorite player never reached the championship series.

"Dear Caitlin Clark Mob, First of all, congratulations!!! You did it!!!" Thomas wrote.

"Angel Reese lost in the WNBA Finals!!! I know this must feel like a championship for you all. The celebrations, the victory laps, the obsession with her Game 7 stats. Y'all are something else. But since we’re talking about stats, I had a quick question.

"How many points did Caitlin Clark score in the WNBA Finals? How many assists? How many logo threes?"

Thomas also brought Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham into the discussion, referencing her viral finger-pointing gesture during a heated exchange with DeWanna Bonner earlier in the season.

He suggested that some supporters appeared more interested in Cunningham's personality and social media moments than the basketball itself.

The former Washington Wizards center argued that Reese deserved recognition for helping Atlanta reach the championship round rather than becoming the target of relentless negativity.

Reese finished Game 7 with eight points, 12 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and four turnovers while shooting 3-of-7 from the field.

Dave Portnoy adds fuel to the Angel Reese debate

Thomas wasn't the only prominent personality discussing Reese's performance. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy also took aim at the forward following Atlanta's defeat, continuing his criticism of the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year.

A well-known Clark supporter, Portnoy shared footage highlighting Reese's struggles and questioned the argument that she deserved consideration for the Finals MVP award.

He particularly focused on her production during the Dream's final three defeats.

According to Portnoy , Reese managed just 23 points on 7-of-27 shooting, converting approximately 25% of her attempts. He also highlighted her eight successful free throws from 13 attempts and 13 turnovers across those games.

Portnoy described her performances as a complete disaster, arguing that criticism shouldn't automatically be dismissed as personal dislike. He also pointed to her limited scoring contributions in Games 4, 5 and 7, when Atlanta desperately needed offensive production.

Nevertheless, Reese's overall Finals contribution deserves context. She averaged 14.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 3.0 assists throughout the series, alongside 1.3 steals and 1.3 blocks per game.

Her defensive presence and rebounding remained important components of Atlanta's championship run.

Golden State ultimately secured its first championship after winning the deciding contest 68-63, ending Atlanta's hopes of lifting the trophy.

The contrasting reactions from Thomas and Portnoy underline how divisive the WNBA's biggest personalities have become.

With the 2026 season now over, the debate surrounding Reese , Clark and their respective supporters doesn't appear to be slowing down anytime soon.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham hires 24/7 security amid FBI stalker watchlist reveal
articles.standfirst: Cunningham reveals why she can no longer enjoy everyday activities without security
articles.summary: Cunningham reveals why she can no longer enjoy everyday activities without security
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham has revealed that she's taking additional steps to protect herself, confirming that she's hired a private security team to accompany her around the clock amid growing concerns about unwanted attention.

The 30-year-old guard discussed the decision on her No Hesitation podcast, explaining that her rising profile has dramatically changed her everyday experiences. While she was previously recognised mainly in certain locations, her growing popularity means she's now attracting attention wherever she goes.

Cunningham admitted that the situation has made ordinary activities increasingly difficult, prompting her to arrange constant personal protection.

“In certain places, people kind of knew who I was and I couldn't really go anywhere,” said Cunningham .

“Now it doesn't matter what state, what city, it's everywhere. And so I've definitely hired security and they're going to start traveling with me actually next week, 24/7. And so that's a little different.

“But yeah, it just kind of stops you from your regular routine. You have to find a balance of getting away and making sure that you're filling up your own cup and doing what you're supposed to.

“So when you're out, you're able to give people your best energy too because that's super important to me. It's just being nice and being positive and treating people with how you wish I could be treated.”

Her announcement follows concerning comments about stalking incidents involving WNBA players. During an appearance on Theo Von's podcast last month, Cunningham revealed that she believed approximately 20 individuals were being monitored by the FBI in connection with potential threats against her.

The FBI hasn't publicly confirmed the reported number, meaning the figure remains based on Cunningham's own account.

FBI investigation and stalking concerns behind Cunningham's security decision

One individual connected to the allegations is Kevin Singh , who is currently being held in an Indiana detention center while facing charges including felony stalking, felony intimidation and misdemeanor harassment.

Singh has pleaded not guilty, and the allegations haven't been proven in court.

Cunningham previously discussed the frightening nature of unwanted attention, explaining that stalking is an unfortunate reality for some professional basketball players. She also revealed that one individual had already been taken into custody.

Interestingly, the Fever guard owns a pet donkey named Kevin , prompting her to jokingly question whether she should change the animal's name following the revelation about the alleged stalker.

Cunningham's growing public profile has coincided with an eventful period in her career. Her performances alongside Caitlin Clark in Indiana have helped establish her as a recognizable WNBA personality, while her outspoken views have also generated considerable discussion.

Earlier this year, she attracted attention following comments about transgender athletes competing in women's sports. Her position sparked debate across the basketball community and brought additional scrutiny to her public appearances.

Meanwhile, uncertainty surrounds her professional future as the 2026 WNBA offseason begins. Cunningham is approaching free agency, leaving questions about whether she'll return to Indiana for another season.

Her immediate priority appears to be personal safety. By arranging round-the-clock protection, Cunningham hopes to regain some normality while continuing her basketball career and public engagements.

articles.title: A reality check from the WNBA Finals: Can Angel Reese no longer be placed on the same level as Caitlin Clark?
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese's late-season struggles raise fresh questions about her standing among the WNBA's biggest stars
articles.summary: Angel Reese's late-season struggles raise fresh questions about her standing among the WNBA's biggest stars
articles.body:
Angel Reese's impressive 2026 campaign ended in disappointment, and her performances during the WNBA Finals have reignited the debate surrounding her standing compared with Caitlin Clark.

Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy has now weighed in, questioning whether Reese deserves to be discussed in the same category as the Indiana Fever superstar.

Speaking on Monday's episode of Wake Up Barstool, Portnoy openly acknowledged his support for Clark before delivering a harsh assessment of Reese's performances in Atlanta's championship defeat against the Golden State Valkyries.

The Dream initially appeared poised to capture the championship after taking a 2-1 series advantage. However, Golden State recovered to win the series 4-3, claiming the title. Reese's declining offensive production became a major talking point as Atlanta struggled to finish the job.

She was outstanding during the opening three games, averaging 21.7 points and 13.3 rebounds while shooting 56.4% from the field. Her production subsequently dropped considerably, with Reese averaging just 9.5 points and shooting 26.7% over the final four contests. She also committed 4.8 turnovers per game during that stretch.

Reese managed only eight points in both Games 4 and 7, while recording seven points in Game 5. Although she bounced back with 15 points and 14 rebounds in Game 6 to help Atlanta force a deciding contest, her offensive struggles returned when the championship was on the line.

"She is a very loud talker when things are going well," Portnoy said. "You can sculpt this any way you want. In the last three losses that they had, she didn’t show up at all.

“Not even a little bit. Not even a tiny bit. ... She made the Finals, congrats, but she lost them the Finals. There’s absolutely no other way to extrapolate this.

Dave Portnoy identifies the moment that changed the series

Portnoy also pointed towards Reese's animated celebrations during Atlanta's Game 3 victory as a possible turning point. Following the Dream's convincing 97-71 win, Reese was visibly confident, having recorded 21 points and 12 rebounds.

According to Portnoy , the celebrations and confidence after taking a 2-1 lead made the subsequent collapse particularly striking. He suggested that Atlanta's momentum disappeared when Golden State began responding. He also praised Gabby Williams , who earned Finals MVP honors, for her spectacular performances throughout the series.

However, Reese's disappointing finish shouldn't erase everything she accomplished throughout the season. She averaged 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals during the regular season, earning Defensive Player of the Year recognition, an All-WNBA Second Team selection and All-Defensive First Team honors.

The forward also helped Atlanta reach its first Finals since 2013, an achievement worth recognizing despite the heartbreaking conclusion. Reese expressed gratitude towards her teammates after the defeat, insisting that the Dream would return stronger.

Meanwhile, Reese has announced plans to step away from her podcasts during the offseason, explaining that she's dedicating the break to herself. She'll use the time to recover and prepare for another championship push.
